title: Corvette ZR1 vs Ferrari 296 GTB: The Difference Nobody Explains

scenes.text: Two rear-engine supercars, both with twin turbochargers, both with eight-speed dual-clutch gearboxes, both rear-wheel drive. One has a five point five litre V eight and one thousand, sixty-four horsepower. The other has a three litre V six, an electric motor, and a prancing horse on the nose. In a drag race filmed in December, the cheaper one won both runs. This is the real difference between the Corvette ZR1 and the Ferrari two ninety-six G T B.
scenes.query: Chevrolet Corvette ZR1 and Ferrari 296 GTB
scenes.caption: CORVETTE ZR1 VS FERRARI 296 GTB: THE DIFFERENCE NOBODY EXPLAINS

scenes.text: Here is the twist. In the drag race, the Corvette won by about four tenths of a second. But the race was a single video with no stated conditions, the Ferrari makes a very different kind of car, and the price gap, on the figures we found, is much larger than the headlines suggest. We will go through the numbers, and say where the sources disagree.
scenes.caption: THE ZR1 WON BOTH RUNS · BUT READ THE FINE PRINT

scenes.text: Every figure comes from a published source, listed in the description. Where sources disagree, we tell you. Where we do the maths ourselves, we say so. And where a number is a manufacturer's claim rather than a measurement, we label it as one.
scenes.caption: EVERY NUMBER IS SOURCED

scenes.text: Start with what each car is. Wikipedia says the Corvette ZR1 is the top variant of the C8 range, with a five point five litre L T seven twin-turbocharged flat-plane crank V eight. Production and ordering began in spring twenty twenty-five. The C8 itself is GM's first rear mid-engine sports car since the Pontiac Fiero, and the first mid-engine Corvette.
scenes.caption: ZR1: 5.5 L TWIN-TURBO FLAT-PLANE V8 · ORDERS FROM SPRING 2025
scenes.chapter: Two different ideas of a mid-engine car

scenes.text: The Ferrari two ninety-six G T B was unveiled on the twenty-fourth of June, twenty twenty-one, with sales starting in twenty twenty-two, Wikipedia says. It uses a three litre, one hundred twenty degree twin-turbo V six, the F one sixty-three B C, plus an electric motor and a seven point four five kilowatt-hour battery. The page calls it the first real Ferrari with just six cylinders.
scenes.caption: 296 GTB: UNVEILED JUNE 24, 2021 · 3.0 L TWIN-TURBO V6 + ELECTRIC MOTOR · 7.45 KWH BATTERY

scenes.text: The name tells you the recipe. Wikipedia says the two nine six follows the original Dino scheme, which indicates displacement and cylinder count: two point nine litres, six cylinders. It also notes the page itself gives the engine as two thousand, nine hundred ninety-two cubic centimetres, three point oh litres, in one place, and two point nine in the Speciale section. A small discrepancy, but a real one.
scenes.caption: '296' = 2.9 L, 6 CYLINDERS (DINO SCHEME) · PAGE ALSO GIVES 2,992 CC / 3.0 L

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, the Corvette's engine is about eighty-four percent larger, five point five litres against two thousand, nine hundred ninety-two cubic centimetres. The Corvette has eight cylinders, the Ferrari six. The Corvette is purely petrol, the Ferrari is a plug-in hybrid. They are aimed at the same kind of buyer, but built on completely different ideas of how to get there.
scenes.caption: ZR1 ENGINE ≈ 84% LARGER · V8 PETROL vs V6 PLUG-IN HYBRID (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: The Corvette ZR1 is rated at one thousand, sixty-four horsepower at seven thousand r p m and eight hundred twenty-eight pound-feet at six thousand, according to Wikipedia. The Ferrari's combined output is eight hundred thirty metric horsepower, which the page converts to eight hundred nineteen horsepower, with seven hundred forty newton-metres, or five hundred forty-six pound-feet, at six thousand, two hundred fifty r p m.
scenes.caption: ZR1: 1,064 HP / 828 LB-FT · 296 GTB: 830 PS (819 HP) / 546 LB-FT (WIKIPEDIA)

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, the Corvette has about thirty percent more power, one thousand, sixty-four over eight hundred nineteen, and about fifty-two percent more torque, eight hundred twenty-eight over five hundred forty-six. Motor One lists the Ferrari at eight hundred twenty horsepower, so the sources differ by one. That is rounding, not a contradiction. The size of the gap is not in doubt.
scenes.caption: ZR1 HAS ~30% MORE POWER AND ~52% MORE TORQUE (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Where does the Ferrari's power come from? Wikipedia says the V six makes six hundred sixty-three metric horsepower at eight thousand r p m on its own, and the electric motor adds one hundred sixty-seven, with three hundred fifteen newton-metres. By our arithmetic, the engine alone makes about two hundred twenty-two metric horsepower per litre, against about one hundred ninety-three horsepower per litre for the Corvette.
scenes.caption: V6 ALONE: 663 PS AT 8,000 RPM · +167 PS ELECTRIC · ~222 PS/L vs ZR1 ~193 HP/L (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Note the units, though: we compared metric horsepower for the Ferrari with horsepower for the Corvette, which are not identical, and the difference is about one and a half percent. We keep the figure because the gap in specific output is larger than that, but treat it as approximate. The Ferrari is the high-revving small engine, the Corvette the big boosted one.
scenes.caption: METRIC VS MECHANICAL HP DIFFER BY ~1.5% — TREAT AS APPROXIMATE

scenes.text: Weight is where our sources run thin. Wikipedia gives the ZR1 a curb weight of three thousand, eight hundred thirty-one pounds in its infobox, and a dry weight of three thousand, six hundred seventy pounds, one thousand, six hundred sixty kilograms, in the text. The convertible's dry weight is three thousand, seven hundred fifty-eight. By our arithmetic, the curb weight is about one thousand, seven hundred thirty-eight kilograms.
scenes.caption: ZR1: 3,831 LB CURB (1,738 KG, OUR CONVERSION) · 3,670 LB DRY · CONVERTIBLE 3,758 LB DRY
scenes.chapter: Round two: weight and the numbers we do not have

scenes.text: For the Ferrari two ninety-six G T B, the Wikipedia page we used gives no weight. It gives a power-to-weight figure of five hundred sixty horsepower per ton. If that is a metric tonne, a guess about the units, the implied weight is about one thousand, four hundred sixty-three kilograms. The Speciale is listed at one thousand, four hundred ten kilograms dry. Without a sourced figure, we do not claim a weight for the standard car.
scenes.caption: 296 GTB WEIGHT: NOT GIVEN · 560 HP/TON IMPLIES ~1,463 KG IF METRIC (OUR GUESS) · SPECIALE 1,410 KG DRY

scenes.text: Motor One says the Ferrari is lighter than the Corvette but does not quantify it. That matches our reading: the Corvette makes much more power, but the Ferrari is the lighter car. By our arithmetic, the ZR1's power to weight at its infobox figure is about six hundred twelve horsepower per metric tonne. The Ferrari's is five hundred sixty by the page's own figure. So the Corvette still leads on that measure.
scenes.caption: ZR1 ~612 HP/TONNE (OUR ARITHMETIC) vs 296 GTB 560 HP/TON (WIKIPEDIA)

scenes.text: Both cars have a dual-clutch gearbox with eight speeds and rear-wheel drive, according to Motor One. Wikipedia describes the Ferrari's electric motor as part of a plug-in hybrid system, and quotes an electric range of twenty-five kilometres, sixteen miles. Kelley Blue Book, by contrast, estimates an electric range of seven miles. That is a large gap between sources, and we do not know which basis each uses.
scenes.caption: ELECTRIC RANGE: 25 KM / 16 MI (WIKIPEDIA) VS 7 MI (KBB)

scenes.text: The Ferrari's electric motor changes how it behaves, and what it needs. Kelley Blue Book lists a charge time of two and a half hours on a two hundred forty volt supply, and a combined fuel economy of eighteen miles per gallon. The Corvette's economy is not in our sources. We include these figures because buyers of cars like these rarely ask, but a plug-in hybrid comes with a charging cable.
scenes.caption: 296 GTB: 240 V CHARGE ~2.5 H · 18 MPG COMBINED (KBB)

scenes.text: The Ferrari first. Wikipedia says zero to a hundred kilometres per hour in two point nine seconds, and a top speed over three hundred thirty kilometres per hour, two hundred five miles per hour. Both are manufacturer claims. The page gives no Fiorano lap time, and no zero to two hundred figure. Kelley Blue Book also gives two hundred five miles per hour for the top speed.
scenes.caption: 296 GTB (CLAIMED): 0–100 KM/H 2.9 S · OVER 330 KM/H (205 MPH)
scenes.chapter: Round three: speed, in claims and measurements

scenes.text: Now the Corvette. Wikipedia says Chevrolet claims zero to sixty in two point five seconds, or two point three with the ZTK package, a quarter mile of nine point seven, and a top speed of two hundred thirty-three miles per hour, tested by GM president Mark Reuss. Car and Driver, via The Drive, measured two point two seconds and nine point five at one hundred forty-nine miles per hour.
scenes.caption: ZR1: CLAIMED 2.5 S / 2.3 S ZTK · 9.7 S · 233 MPH (REUSS) · C&D 2.2 S, 9.5 S AT 149 MPH

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, the Ferrari's two point nine seconds to a hundred kilometres per hour is a little different from zero to sixty, since sixty miles per hour is about ninety-seven kilometres per hour. A time to sixty would be marginally shorter. Even so, it is clear that the Corvette's measured two point two and the Ferrari's claimed two point nine are a long way apart, though one is measured and one is a claim.
scenes.caption: CORVETTE MEASURED 2.2 S TO 60 MPH vs FERRARI CLAIMED 2.9 S TO 100 KM/H (DIFFERENT UNITS, CLAIM VS TEST)

scenes.text: The top speeds are the other way round in terms of caution. The Ferrari's two hundred five miles per hour is a claim, with no test cited. The Corvette's two hundred thirty-three is stated as tested, but by the head of the company that makes it. By our arithmetic, that is about fourteen percent faster on paper. We would want an independent test of both before drawing conclusions.
scenes.caption: ZR1 233 MPH (TESTED BY GM'S PRESIDENT) vs 296 GTB 205 MPH (CLAIMED) ≈ +14% (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: The race that went viral. Motor One reports, on the twenty-eighth of December, twenty twenty-five, a quarter-mile drag race between a Corvette ZR1 and a Ferrari two ninety-six G T B, filmed by the YouTube channel DragTimes. The article does not state the track, the weather, the surface or the drivers. It is a single video, and the times are not independently verified.
scenes.caption: DEC 28, 2025: ZR1 vs 296 GTB QUARTER-MILE (DRAGTIMES VIDEO, REPORTED BY MOTOR1) · CONDITIONS NOT STATED

scenes.text: The results. Run one: the Corvette ran nine point two nine one seconds at one hundred fifty-three point two oh miles per hour, the Ferrari nine point seven three seven seconds at one hundred forty-six point oh eight. Run two: the Corvette nine point three one five at one hundred fifty-one point seven, the Ferrari nine point seven four five at one hundred forty-five point six six. The Corvette won both.
scenes.caption: RUN 1: ZR1 9.291 S / 153.20 MPH · 296 9.737 S / 146.08 · RUN 2: ZR1 9.315 / 151.70 · 296 9.745 / 145.66

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, the gap was four hundred forty-six milliseconds on the first run and four hundred thirty on the second, about four and a half percent of the Ferrari's time. In trap speed, the Corvette was about seven miles per hour faster at the end of the quarter mile, around five percent. Those are consistent results across two runs, which is a point in their favour.
scenes.caption: GAP: 0.446 S AND 0.430 S (~4.5%) · TRAP SPEED +7.1 AND +6.0 MPH (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: A drag race from a standing start suits a car with a lot of power, a lot of torque, and rear tyres sized for traction. The Drive says the ZR1's wide rear tyres were a factor in its launch. The Ferrari has a lot of low-end punch too, thanks to its electric motor, but a smaller engine and less total output. This race is not a measure of everything a car does.
scenes.caption: A DRAG RACE FAVOURS POWER AND TRACTION · IT IS NOT A LAP TIME

scenes.text: Which brings us to a gap in the record. Our sources give a Nürburgring time for the Corvette, six minutes, fifty point seven six three seconds, according to Wikipedia. They give none for the Ferrari two ninety-six G T B, and no Fiorano time either. So we cannot compare the two on a circuit, which is a better test of a mid-engine car than a straight line. We will not guess.
scenes.caption: ZR1: 6:50.763 AT THE NÜRBURGRING · 296 GTB: NO LAP TIME IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: Now the money. Wikipedia lists the ZR1 at one hundred seventy-three thousand, three hundred dollars for the 1LZ coupe and one hundred eighty-four thousand, three hundred for the 3LZ. Car and Driver, quoted by The Drive and AOL, gives a starting price of about one hundred seventy-five thousand. Motor One says one hundred eighty-five thousand, which it says can reach the low two hundred thousands with options.
scenes.caption: ZR1: $173,300 (1LZ) · $184,300 (3LZ) · ~$175K (C&D) · $185K (MOTOR1)

scenes.text: For the Ferrari, Motor One says three hundred fifty thousand dollars. Kelley Blue Book lists an original M S R P of three hundred thirty-eight thousand, two hundred fifty-five dollars for a twenty twenty-four model, and a fair purchase price of three hundred one thousand dollars. Again, three sources, three numbers. Ferraris are rarely sold at a single price, because options and dealer allocations vary.
scenes.caption: 296 GTB: $350,000 (MOTOR1) · $338,255 ORIGINAL MSRP (KBB, 2024) · $301,000 FAIR PURCHASE (KBB)

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, with the lowest ZR1 figure and the lowest Ferrari figure, the Ferrari's original M S R P of three hundred thirty-eight thousand is about one point nine times the Corvette's one hundred seventy-five thousand. With Motor One's prices, one hundred eighty-five thousand against three hundred fifty thousand, the Ferrari costs about eighty-nine percent more. So the Ferrari costs nearly double.
scenes.caption: 296 GTB ≈ 1.9× THE ZR1 (KBB vs C&D) · +89% (MOTOR1 PRICES) (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Motor One's own wording is inconsistent. It says the ZR1 is about one hundred seventy-five thousand dollars cheaper, but the two prices it states differ by one hundred sixty-five thousand. We use the stated prices, not the wording. It is a small error, but it shows how easily a number drifts in repetition, and why we keep showing where ours comes from.
scenes.caption: MOTOR1: '$175K CHEAPER' vs STATED PRICES $185K / $350K = $165K

scenes.text: Sticker prices are not what everyone pays. GM Authority reported, in June twenty twenty-five, a Monterey, California, dealership listing a ZR1 3LZ with a window sticker of two hundred six thousand, eighty dollars and a one hundred thousand dollar markup. It also reported fifty thousand dollar markups on other allocations. The source for these was a Facebook post, and the article did not verify them.
scenes.caption: JUNE 2025: ZR1 3LZ STICKER $206,080 + $100K MARKUP · OTHERS +$50K (GM AUTHORITY, UNVERIFIED)

scenes.text: A Reddit user quoted by the same article said he contacted every Chevrolet dealer within three hundred miles of Chicago, and only one agreed to list him at no markup; the biggest he saw was one hundred fifty thousand dollars over sticker. In December, GM Authority reported that some dealers were not marking up, listing two thousand twenty-six ZR1s from one hundred ninety-nine thousand, eighty-five dollars.
scenes.caption: DEC 2025: SOME DEALERS AT STICKER (EL PASO $199,085) · OTHERS ASKING $320K–$340K

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, a ZR1 with a one hundred thousand dollar markup on a two hundred six thousand dollar sticker would cost about three hundred six thousand dollars, which GM Authority does not state. That would be close to the three hundred one thousand dollar fair purchase price Kelley Blue Book lists for the Ferrari. The price advantage depends heavily on whether you pay sticker, and our sources show that varied by dealer.
scenes.caption: $206,080 + $100,000 = $306,080 (OUR ARITHMETIC) vs 296 GTB KBB FAIR PRICE $301,000

scenes.text: The Ferrari also has a smaller advantage in warranty than you might expect. Kelley Blue Book lists a basic and powertrain warranty of three years and unlimited miles. We did not find a sourced Corvette warranty figure for the ZR1, so we do not compare. We mention the Ferrari figure because buyers of expensive cars often ask, and because it is the kind of detail a spec sheet leaves out.
scenes.caption: 296 GTB WARRANTY: 3 YEARS / UNLIMITED MILES (KBB) · ZR1: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: Both cars already have faster siblings. Wikipedia says the Ferrari two ninety-six Speciale, announced in April twenty twenty-five, has a V six tuned to seven hundred metric horsepower, a system output of eight hundred eighty, a dry weight of one thousand, four hundred ten kilograms for the coupe, and a claimed twenty percent more downforce than the base model. Those are all claims.
scenes.caption: 296 SPECIALE (APR 2025): 700 PS ENGINE · 880 PS SYSTEM · 1,410 KG DRY · +20% DOWNFORCE (CLAIMED)
scenes.chapter: The Speciale and the ZR1X: the next round

scenes.text: The Corvette answer is the ZR1X, with the same twin-turbo V eight plus an upgraded E-Ray electric motor on the front axle, for one thousand, two hundred fifty horsepower and all-wheel drive. Wikipedia lists a Nürburgring time of six forty-nine point two seven five, and says Chevrolet claims under two seconds to sixty and a quarter mile under nine seconds. Those are claims, not tests.
scenes.caption: ZR1X: 1,250 HP · AWD · NÜRBURGRING 6:49.275 · CLAIMED <2 S TO 60, <9 S QUARTER

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, the ZR1X's system output is about forty-four percent above the Speciale's eight hundred sixty-eight horsepower, converted from eight hundred eighty metric. Even among the faster cars, the Corvette keeps a big power lead. The Ferrari's answer is lower weight and more downforce. Whether that wins on a circuit depends on data we do not have, so we stay away from predictions.
scenes.caption: ZR1X 1,250 vs SPECIALE 868 HP = +44% (OUR ARITHMETIC) · NO LAP DATA FOR THE FERRARI

scenes.text: Price per horsepower is a crude measure, but it makes the gap concrete. By our arithmetic, at one hundred seventy-three thousand, three hundred dollars, the ZR1 costs about one hundred sixty-three dollars per horsepower. At three hundred thirty-eight thousand, two hundred fifty-five dollars, the Ferrari costs about four hundred thirteen dollars per horsepower, using Wikipedia's eight hundred nineteen. That is about two and a half times as much.
scenes.caption: ZR1 ≈ $163/HP · 296 GTB ≈ $413/HP ≈ 2.5× (OUR ARITHMETIC)
scenes.chapter: What the spec sheets leave out

scenes.text: With Motor One's prices, the numbers shift but the picture does not. One hundred eighty-five thousand over one thousand, sixty-four horsepower is about one hundred seventy-four dollars per horsepower for the Corvette. Three hundred fifty thousand over eight hundred twenty is about four hundred twenty-seven for the Ferrari. Different prices, same conclusion. Power per dollar is not what the Ferrari is selling.
scenes.caption: MOTOR1 PRICES: ZR1 ≈ $174/HP · 296 GTB ≈ $427/HP (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: What is the Ferrari selling? Partly an engine that revs to eight thousand r p m, partly the badge, partly a hybrid system that Wikipedia says includes a seven point four five kilowatt-hour battery. Compare that with the Corvette E-Ray, a different Corvette, whose battery the page gives as one point nine kilowatt-hours. By our arithmetic, the Ferrari's battery is nearly four times as large, and the ZR1 has no battery at all.
scenes.caption: 296 GTB BATTERY 7.45 KWH vs E-RAY 1.9 KWH (≈3.9×) · ZR1: NONE (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Size. Kelley Blue Book lists the Ferrari two ninety-six at one hundred seventy-nine point seven inches long, with a wheelbase of one hundred two point four and a width with mirrors of seventy-seven point one, and a fuel tank of seventeen point two gallons. We did not find sourced dimensions for the ZR1, so we leave the comparison there. Spec sheets are rarely complete, and ours are no exception.
scenes.caption: 296 GTB: 179.7 IN LONG · 102.4 IN WHEELBASE · 77.1 IN WIDE · 17.2 GAL TANK (KBB)

scenes.text: Open-top versions. Wikipedia says the Ferrari two ninety-six G T S has a folding hardtop that takes fourteen seconds to operate and works up to forty-five kilometres per hour. It weighs seventy kilograms more than the G T B, with equal claimed performance. The Corvette ZR1 convertible has a dry weight of three thousand, seven hundred fifty-eight pounds, eighty-eight pounds more than the coupe, by our arithmetic.
scenes.caption: 296 GTS: HARDTOP IN 14 S · +70 KG · ZR1 CONVERTIBLE: +88 LB DRY (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Track versions. Wikipedia says the Ferrari offers an Assetto Fiorano pack with upgraded suspension, carbon-fibre bodywork and a polycarbonate rear window, but gives no figures. The Corvette's track-focused version is the ZR1X, with a carbon-fibre splitter, dive planes and a high-downforce rear wing, and Alcon carbon-ceramic brakes with ten-piston front calipers, which Chevrolet claims give one point nine g of deceleration from one-eighty to one-twenty.
scenes.query: Ferrari Assetto Fiorano and Corvette ZR1X
scenes.caption: ASSETTO FIORANO PACK (NO FIGURES) · ZR1X: SPLITTER, DIVE PLANES, WING, ALCON 10-PISTON BRAKES (1.9 G CLAIMED)

scenes.text: There is also a difference in heritage. Wikipedia says the C8 is the first mid-engine Corvette, and that development began around twenty sixteen for a car originally planned for the twenty eighteen model year. The two ninety-six, by contrast, is described as the first real Ferrari with just six cylinders. In both cases, the company broke with its own tradition to build the car. That is the common thread.
scenes.caption: BOTH BROKE WITH TRADITION: FIRST MID-ENGINE CORVETTE · FIRST REAL SIX-CYLINDER FERRARI

scenes.text: And a note on the headlines. Many articles about this race said the Corvette humiliated a Ferrari. The source we found is more careful: two runs, one video, no stated conditions, and a note that the one thousand, two hundred fifty horsepower ZR1X was not tested. We think the fair reading is that a ZR1 is faster in a straight line, and costs a lot less, which the numbers support.
scenes.caption: THE SOURCE: TWO RUNS · ONE VIDEO · NO STATED CONDITIONS

scenes.text: What we could not find: a sourced curb weight for the standard two ninety-six, a Fiorano lap time, a verified Corvette warranty, the ZR1's dimensions, or a Nürburgring time for the Ferrari. Without those, a full comparison is not possible. We prefer to say so than to fill the gaps with guesses. If you have a source for any of them, tell us in the comments.
scenes.caption: WHAT OUR SOURCES DO NOT SAY

scenes.text: So, which wins? On power and torque, the Corvette. On measured drag racing, the Corvette, on the one video we have. On price, the Corvette, by a wide margin, unless you pay a large markup. On engine efficiency per litre, the Ferrari. On electric driving, the Ferrari, since the Corvette has none. On lap times, we have no Ferrari data, so we decline to say.
scenes.caption: SCORECARD

scenes.text: The real difference is the philosophy. Chevrolet used a big engine, two turbochargers and lots of tyre to deliver the most power it could for the money. Ferrari used a small, high-revving V six with an electric motor to deliver a different kind of speed, at a different price. Both reached similar speeds by very different routes. That is our reading of the numbers above.
scenes.caption: BIG ENGINE AND TYRES vs SMALL ENGINE AND ELECTRIC MOTOR (OUR READING)

scenes.text: A caution. We have not driven either car. The drag race is a single video, the Ferrari's weight is not in our sources, several prices disagree, and some comparisons are our own arithmetic. We have tried to say so each time. If you have a verified figure, put it in the comments, with where it comes from.
scenes.caption: NUMBERS, NOT A DRIVING VERDICT

scenes.text: Which would you rather have in your garage, the Corvette or the Ferrari? Tell us in the comments. In the other videos of this series, we reveal two things you may not know about the ZR1, ask whether a normal person can afford one, and tell the story of America's fastest Corvette. Our twenty twenty-seven Truck Buyer's Guide is linked in the description. Subscribe to Pickup Reality.
scenes.caption: SUBSCRIBE: PICKUP REALITY
